title: Empirical investigation of locally made biodiesel on the automobile properties of diesel engine
author: Emetere, Adejumo, et al.

steps.title: Extract palm oil
steps.instruction: Place palm biomass in an expeller or mechanical press and collect the extracted oil.

steps.title: Remove water from oil
steps.instruction: Transfer the oil to a Soxhlet extractor, heat with a heating mantle, boil the oil to about 110 °C to eliminate water, then allow it to cool to 40 °C.

steps.title: Prepare methoxide solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.4 g of concentrated NaOH in 20 mL of methanol (alkanol).

steps.title: Transesterification reaction
steps.instruction: Add the methoxide to the cooled oil, regulate the mixture temperature to 60 °C, and stir continuously for 2 hours.

steps.title: Phase separation
steps.instruction: Pour the reaction mixture into a separation flask and let it stand for 24 hours; biodiesel will form the upper layer and glycerin will settle at the bottom.

steps.title: Wash biodiesel
steps.instruction: Wash the separated biodiesel about five times to remove residual glycerin.

steps.title: UV characterization
steps.instruction: Characterize the washed biodiesel using a UV spectrometer at wavelengths 500 nm, 600 nm, 700 nm, 800 nm, and 900 nm.

steps.title: Measure viscosity
steps.instruction: Heat the biodiesel to a constant 40 °C in a viscometer bath tube and measure viscosity using a viscometer with a C value of 7.870 mm²/s.

steps.title: Prepare fuel blends
steps.instruction: Mix 10 % biodiesel with 90 % pure diesel to obtain B10, and mix 20 % biodiesel with 80 % diesel to obtain B20; measure each blend with a measuring cylinder and place each in a 1 L bottle.

steps.title: Engine testing of blends
steps.instruction: Feed the B10 and B20 blends into the TD 200 test‑bed engine, set engine speeds to 2000, 2150, 2169, 2172, 2193, 2200, and 2500 revolutions per second, and record torque, rotational speed, differential pressure, operational temperature, and power generated at each speed.

steps.title: Control and secondary calculations
steps.instruction: Run pure diesel as a control under the same conditions; derive secondary datasets (horsepower, thermal efficiency, normal engine efficiency, brake mean effective pressure) mathematically from the initial measurements.

steps.title: Measure engine sound
steps.instruction: Measure the sound of the engine for each fuel (pure diesel, B10, B20) using a sound level meter.

steps.title: Collect data display
steps.instruction: Obtain the full dataset from the TQ data display unit.

steps.title: Simulate results
steps.instruction: Carry out simulation of the experimental data using Matlab and CERN Root.

description: 500 nm wavelength was selected as the control value during the characterization of the biodiesel produce (using UV spectrophotometer). This idea is to comprehend the changes of the cyclic breaking nature of biodiesel products as postulated in ref [3,4]. The determination of the cyclic breaking in biodiesel depends on the number of clear peaks in the absorption spectra. Sometimes excessive (unclear) peaks indicate the error due to noise in the biodiesel product.
